notes:
• Workspace list: a PR whose checks are still running shows a yellow icon and "Checks running" (iPhone, Android, Mac), instead of the gray "PR open". New `checks-pending` state from the host; older apps keep showing "PR open".
• Front Desk: it can now look into a chat's queue (the messages that wait until the agent's turn is over) and change it by voice: say what's still waiting, rewrite a queued message, or take one out again, as the queue tray in the apps does. New ones still go in as before ("schick ihm danach noch …"). Changes go out after the announcement and the usual moment for "Stopp", and only if the message is still waiting then; the queue in the apps updates right away. When it reads a chat, queued messages no longer look like ones the agent has already read.
• Mac: the chat's text size can be changed, in Settings → Appearance → Chat text size (80–200 %) or with ⌘+, ⌘− and ⌘0 (View menu). It scales messages and replies, including code blocks and tables. Phones keep the system's text size.
• Mac: "Test devices" in the sidebar under Search and the dashboards: the Android test devices with alias, who has each and how many watch, and the one you pick live next to them, as on the iPhone, iPad and Android. A chat's `dh` commands get "Watch live", and a `dh handoff` a card with the agent's note and "Watch live": both open the device live in a tab of the right panel next to the chat.
• Activity pills sit right above the message box again instead of high over it, and the box grows with a long message again instead of its text running under the model picker (iPhone, iPad and the Mac). On the Mac a pill's command is cut shorter, and its tooltip with the whole command comes after a moment instead of a second or two.
• A Claude chat whose conversation Claude Code can no longer find (cleaned up or deleted) now says so and starts a new Claude session on the next message, instead of failing every send.
• Front Desk: the voice now knows exactly what each chat does and since when ("arbeitet seit 14:02", "fertig seit 13:40"), what waits in its queue (and which of it came from the call), and what the call has sent that hasn't reached the agent yet, so it no longer calls a chat done and then working without saying why. Messages still waiting in a chat's queue no longer read as if the agent had them. Host only; the apps are unchanged.
• The Front Desk asks "Was kann ich noch für dich tun?" only once, when it's through with what was up at the start of the call, instead of after nearly every instruction, result, news item or thanks. After those it now stays quiet until you speak. A style you edited yourself keeps its own wording.
• Mac: ⌘⇧M mutes and unmutes the Front Desk call in every app, not only while Stellwerk is in front. Other apps don't get ⌘⇧M during the call; Settings → Front Desk → "Mute shortcut in every app" turns it off. No permission needed. iPhone and Android are unchanged (the iPhone mutes through CallKit and the AirPods' stem).
• Mac window: the bars at the chat's top right and their list show every prompt of the chat right away, not only the ones loaded so far. A click on an older one loads the chat back to it and jumps there. Only the Mac window has this list, so the iPhone and Android apps don't change; Android's models know the new field.
• Test devices on the Mac: ⌘V on a device's live view pastes the Mac's clipboard on the device, and 📋 does too (it couldn't read the clipboard in the app before).
• Test devices: right after Stellwerk started, a device's live view could tell you that you yourself had the device ("… has it, tap Take over") as soon as you tapped it. On a private host you are now the same person before and after Stellwerk learns your GitHub login.
• Builds with Xcode 27 and the iOS 27 SDK.
